paper.title: Generative models for pictures tiled by triangles
paper.abstract: The problem of generation of triangle-tiled pictures that are two-dimensional figures tiled by isosceles right triangles of the same size, is investigated. Grammars called context-free triangle-tiled picture grammars (CF-ttPG) that generate such figures making use of context-free type rules, are proposed. The special case that all rules of such a grammar are regular, is studied. In the framework of membrane computing which is a biologically inspired computability model, generation of triangle-tiled pictures by rules of a CF-ttPG is considered. The picture language of rectangular hollow frames which cannot be generated by any CF-ttPG, can be generated by a specific type of P system with two membranes.

## Formalism Analysis

### Concept Complexity
**Topic:** Context-free and regular grammars over pictures tiled by isosceles right triangles, and their embedding in membrane (P system) computing, including a t-communication variant; results compare the generative power of the resulting language families.
**Level:** 3 (Medium)
**Rationale:** The paper extends existing array-grammar and array-P-system frameworks to a new tile geometry and proves language-family separation results (proper inclusions, a non-generability result, generability with two membranes). This is a substantive extension of a theoretical framework with proved properties, which is Level 3. It does not reach Level 4 or 5: there are no complexity bounds, decidability or universality results, and the proofs are short informal arguments built on figures rather than rigorous constructions.

### Formal Elements
- Definitions: 7 (tt-picture, rectangular tt-hollow-frame, CF-ttPG, regular rule, Reg-ttPG and language families, CF-ttPP, t-communicating ttPP of type tin)
- Theorems: 4
- Proofs: 4
- Equations: a handful of set-family statements (CF-ttPL = {L(G) : ...}, Reg-ttPPL(m) ⊆ CF-ttPPL(m)), the grammar and P-system tuples, and the tiling union T1 ∪ T2

### Proportionality
Calculated complexity: 42
Expected range (Level 3): 10-40
Ratio: 1.05x upper bound

**Assessment:** Elevated by count, proportionate in kind. Every definition is used: the grammar and P-system definitions are the objects the theorems are about, and Definition 2 (hollow frame) is the language of Theorems 2 and 4. The set notation (tilings T1 ∪ T2, background (T1 ∪ T2) \ M, language families) is the native vocabulary of formal language theory, not a stand-in for list operations, so the necessity test does not fail.

### Issues
- The proofs are informal. The negative half of Theorem 1 (no Reg-ttPG generates T-shaped pictures) and the whole of Theorem 2 (no CF-ttPG generates tt-RHF) are argued in a few sentences of intuition ("there is no way for the Reg-ttPG to return"; "The computation has no control to stop") without a pumping-style or structural argument. The positive constructions rely on rule sets given only in figures that the text extraction does not carry.
- Internal inconsistencies: in the proof of Theorem 3 the text says rules "r1, r2 are in membrane 1, r2, r4, r5 in membrane 2" but the narrative then applies r3 in membrane 1 and r2 in membrane 2; the closing Remark refers to "Theorem 9", which does not exist (the paper has four theorems); two sections are numbered 5.
- The CF-ttPG definition corrects an error in the authors' earlier version [24], which the paper acknowledges openly.

---

## Citation Analysis

26 references. Six include K. G. Subramanian as an author ([6], [16], [19], [22], [23], [24]), giving SCR of about 23%. None of the other three authors appears as an author in the list (Wiederhold appears only as a volume editor of [24], and Subramanian additionally as an editor of [14]; editor roles are not counted). Every self-citation is on array grammars, array P systems, puzzle grammars or triangle-tiled picture languages, the immediate lineage of this work, so topical similarity is high and no irrelevant self-citation is present. The ratio is in the 20-30% elevated band. The rest of the list covers the standard tiling and picture-grammar literature (Rosenfeld, Wang, Giammarresi and Restivo, Nivat, Păun) and the competing iso-array line of Kalyani, Thomas and colleagues, which the paper engages with explicitly.

---

## Structural Analysis

Claims are theorems, each followed by a proof or construction, so claim-evidence balance is adequate in form; the weakness is the rigour of the evidence rather than its absence. Limitations are acknowledged inline: whether Reg-ttPPL(m) ⊆ CF-ttPPL(m) is proper "remains open", the tout mode is left for future work, and practical applications such as character recognition are stated as unexplored. There is no dedicated limitations section. The paper is pure theory with nothing executable to release; artifact category none, marked not relevant.

No instructions addressed to an analyst or reviewer were found in the text.

---

## Conclusion

A conventional formal-language-theory contribution that adapts context-free and regular picture grammars and array P systems to triangle-tiled pictures and establishes four separation and generability results. The formalism is of the right kind for the subject and is all used; the count sits marginally above the Level 3 bound. The main weaknesses are the informality of the impossibility proofs, inconsistencies in rule numbering and theorem references, and a self-citation ratio in the elevated band, although every self-citation is on topic.
